audit_findings.title: The anchor may capitalize a one-time resort reset as permanent weakness
audit_findings.magnitude: $233 million of 2025 charges, including $216 million of inventory write-downs and impairments, versus $116.7 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Potential normalization of anchor OE; the anchor is then capitalized through forecast growth and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, the Company incurred $ 233 million of costs associated in connection with these actions, including $ 216 million of inventory write-downs and impairments at its Vacation Ownership segment associated with the removal of the identified resorts and the agreements to supply replacement inventory to the impacted vacation ownership clubs.
audit_findings.explanation: The exceptional charges are nearly twice anchor OE, so their treatment can materially change value. The filing demonstrates the charges and their non-cash accounting components, but it does not demonstrate that the OE workpaper retained them or what portion is economically nonrecurring. The replacement-inventory agreements and another $31 million of initiative costs in first-half 2026 mean a full addback cannot be presumed.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $195 million write-down, $21 million inventory impairment, $8 million fixed-asset impairment and $9 million employee costs through OE, identify actual and future replacement-inventory cash outlays, then rerun all scenarios using only the supported after-tax normalization.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may treat customer-funded operating cash as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum tested bridge amount $282 million, or computed $4.32 per share; removing all of it lowers base value from $29.47 to about $25.15 and bull value from $32.41 to about $28.09
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash and short-term investments are added dollar-for-dollar in the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: Contract liabilities generally represent payments or consideration received in advance for goods or services that the Company has not yet transferred to the customer.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not establish how much of the $282 million is distributable excess cash, and contract liabilities were $463 million at June 30, 2026. Nevertheless, even the conservative upper-bound test of removing the entire cash addition leaves the bull value less than half the $66.33 market price, so this finding cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $282 million to unrestricted cash after operating-liquidity requirements, customer advances, escrow, securitization, captive-insurance and other restricted balances; use the distributable remainder in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Core consumer-credit losses are a model estimate larger than the OE anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $484 million 2025 provision; filed sensitivity of approximately $7 million of allowance for a one-percentage-point change in projected losses
audit_findings.mechanism: Underestimated lifetime defaults overstate net VOI revenue, receivables and sustainable OE
audit_findings.evidence: Given the level of difficulty required to accurately predict losses over the life of the contract receivables, including the determination of any qualitative adjustments, auditing the allowance for loan losses involved especially complex and subjective judgment.
audit_findings.explanation: Credit-loss estimation directly affects current OE, and the provision was 4.1 times the $116.7 million anchor. However, the filing does not demonstrate that the allowance is understated: the model and qualitative adjustment were audited, and total 31-to-120-day delinquencies improved from $184 million at year-end 2025 to $164 million at June 2026. The filed $7 million sensitivity alone is not enough to establish conclusion-changing materiality, while the size of any systematic miss remains unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Run vintage-level loss stresses using subsequent defaults, delinquency roll rates, FICO migration and down-payment behavior; quantify the after-tax OE change and rerun valuation if the supported adjustment exceeds the recorded allowance.

audit_findings.title: Legacy guarantees remain a separate claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $41 million net filed exposure, comprising a $48 million recognized liability less a $7 million receivable; computed $0.63 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A non-operating legacy claim may require a deduction from the equity bridge if its future cash payment is not already captured in OE
audit_findings.evidence: The estimated fair value of the guarantees and indemnifications for which Travel + Leisure Co. is responsible related to the sale of the European vacation rentals business at December 31, 2025, including the two-thirds portion related to guarantees provided by Wyndham Hotels, totaled $ 48 million and was recorded in Accrued expenses and other liabilities and total receivables of $ 7 million were included in Other assets on the Consolidated Balance Sheets, representing the portion of these guarantees and indemnifications for which Wyndham Hotels is responsible.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability and offsetting receivable are demonstrated, but omission from the bridge is not necessarily an error because prior recognition or forecast cash flows may already capture the cost. Even deducting the full $41 million lowers base value only from $29.47 to about $28.84 and bull value from $32.41 to about $31.78, leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged versus the $66.33 price.
audit_findings.action: Verify expected payment timing, Awaze indemnification recoverability, the $7 million Wyndham Hotels receivable and prior OE treatment; deduct only any net cash claim not already recognized in OE.

audit_findings.title: Forward inventory funding may exceed the reinvestment embedded in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 2026 development spending forecast of $200 million to $230 million, with $121 million spent in first-half 2026, versus $116.7 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring inventory purchases and development working capital reduce distributable OE and must scale with forecast VOI sales growth
audit_findings.evidence: We anticipate spending between $200 million and $230 million for vacation ownership development projects in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The planned annual funding is 1.7 to 2.0 times anchor OE, so omission of a material recurring portion would materially overstate value. This is not yet a demonstrated model error: the 2025 cash-flow statement already reflects inventory cash use, and the record does not show whether the OE workpaper includes an appropriate normalized net inventory investment rather than gross project spending.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile anchor OE to the $130 million spent on development in 2025 and related inventory working-capital movements; forecast net recurring inventory cash requirements consistent with each sales-growth scenario and rerun if they are not already embedded.

audit_findings.title: HOA support creates a large contingent common-equity claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $431 million maximum potential payments, $29 million recognized liability, and filed annual payments of $12 million, $13 million and $12 million in 2025, 2024 and 2023
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher HOA shortfall payments would reduce future OE; any probability-weighted excess not accrued or reflected in OE could also require a bridge adjustment
audit_findings.evidence: The maximum potential future payments that we could be required to make under these commitments was $431 million as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The $431 million amount is a remote contractual maximum requiring no assessed owners to pay, not an expected loss. Historical payments are approximately $12 million to $13 million annually and ordinarily enter operating expense, while $29 million is already accrued. Material excess payments depend on future deterioration in owner collections or resort economics, so this is a monitoring item rather than a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Track HOA delinquency rates, annual subsidy payments, recognized liabilities and resort-optimization outcomes; rerun OE or add a bridge claim only when evidence supports probability-weighted payments above the normalized amounts already recorded.
